newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends up, underpin by BOJ operations.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends up, underpin by BOJ operations.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended firmer on Wednesday, fuelled by Wall Street and the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) accommodative money policy, dealers said.
Wall Street's firmer close on Tuesday helped the Nikkei 225 June contract break its 18,000 barrier, after which several buy-stop orders propelled it to a high of 18,140, they said.
June settled 100 points up, at 18,045 on a turnover of 10,830 lots.
Dealers said BOJ's unexpected refrain from its regular morning money operations further underpinned the market.
"It just reinforced the market belief BOJ will keep interest rates low and has no intention of changing its accommodative stance," said a Japanese dealer.
On Tuesday, the BOJ drained only 400 billion yen from the market against an estimated 510 billion yen surplus.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract closed at 357.2 against its previous close at 359.2. Turnover was healthy, at 1,098 lots.
